core_obligations: Reduce to primes: the proof writes the spectrum, the closed subset and their completions, and translates the statement into a comparison between corresponding pairs of primes of the ring and of its completion (proof lines 2639-2646)
The first inequality: it compares the depth terms and the dimension terms for corresponding pairs, obtaining the first displayed inequality of the statement (proof lines 2646-2700)

The second inequality under the (S_n) hypothesis: assuming the formal fibres satisfy the Serre condition, the proof shows that the localization at the corresponding pair has at least two primes whenever the cutoff upstairs is small, which yields the min(n+1, .) inequality (proof lines 2700-2743)
Conclusion: the two displayed inequalities of the statement (proof line 2743)
proof_roadmap: 把陈述翻译成 A 与其完备化 A^ 中对应素对 p ⊂ q 上的比较。
逐项比较 depth 与维数项得第一条不等式；再在形式纤维满足 (S_n) 时，说明当上方的 cutoff 小时 (A^/p')_{q'} 至少有两个素理想，从而 min(n+1, s) ≤ s^，即第二条不等式。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement compares the cutoff of a finite module over a universally catenary Noetherian local ring with the cutoff of its completion (author lemma at source lines 2627-2637, label lemma-cutoff-completion), with a second inequality valid when the formal fibres satisfy a Serre condition. The proof (source lines 2639-2743) translates the comparison into one between corresponding pairs of primes in the ring and in its completion, compares the depth and dimension terms to get the first inequality, and then uses the Serre condition on the formal fibres to show that a certain localization has at least two primes, which produces the min(n+1, .) inequality (proof lines 2700-2743). The prime-by-prime comparison and the two-prime argument are the content. H2.
